newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains cattle slow at $71.00 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains cattle slow at $71.00 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $71.00 per cwt, steady with Tuesday, in light volume as feedlots sold most of their remaining cattle offerings for this week, feedlot sources said.
About 1,000 head each were sold in Kansas and the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma areas, USDA said.

With most of this week's showlist reportedly already sold, attention was turning to next week, which some market sources said could see cattle priced at $73.00 to $74.00 and packers bidding $72.00 on continued tight cattle supplies.
Demand for cattle also was seen driven by moderately strong beef demand this week and ideas that light slaughter would contribute to beef price advances, market sources said.
Heavyweight choice beef at midday was quoted up $0.35 per cwt at $105.94, according to USDA. The heavyweight choice price has climbed $1.06 since Friday.

Cattle slaughter Wednesday was estimated at 126,000 head, compared with 131,000 a week ago and 135,000 a year ago, USDA said. The week to date figure was 376,000 head, unchanged from a week ago and down 3.6 percent from a year ago.
